tasks.short: Calculate courses and check masonry alignment

steps.what: Measure the work area and establish dimensions, datum points and course requirements
Calculate angles, course counts and horizontal or vertical offsets from measured inputs
Check calculated courses against the site and determine vertical and horizontal alignment

tasks.design: Use a native construction calculator category in {OTHER} for arithmetic on the brickmason's verified measurements. Keep datum selection, measurement and physical alignment checks fully with the brickmason.
tasks.previous_blocker: Repeated course and offset arithmetic is worked out manually.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing calculators can apply fixed geometry and course formulas.
tasks.still_hard: An incorrect datum or joint assumption makes correct arithmetic unusable.
tasks.human_edge: The brickmason interprets site conditions and checks the physical layout.
tasks.altitude: Less repeated arithmetic; no reduction in site measurement or alignment responsibility.

evidence.claim: Fixed geometry and course arithmetic can use an existing calculator; the task shares and savings are E1 scenarios rather than digest cases.

assumptions: Boundary is layout arithmetic and alignment determination, excluding laying masonry and structural design.

Brickmason produces datum reference, measured runs and rises, angle basis, brick dimensions, joint allowance and units in s1's retained 50 hours, including calculator entry. Missing dimensions or unusual geometry use manual calculation and checks in s3.
Test an existing calculator before custom software. OTHER denotes a construction calculator used in the future. Existing calculator runtime earns no saving.
unknowns: Existing calculator use and allowed tolerances
research_questions: Does calculator use reduce total arithmetic time while retaining all measurement and alignment checks?

already_counted.description: Measurement, datum selection and input capture

incremental.description: Check calculator settings and representative geometry cases

approvals.approved_version: Exact datum, measured dimensions, course layout and verified site alignment; changed inputs require recheck

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=80; gross 20 less 4 upkeep gives net 16. Low assumes a calculator already handles the arithmetic and no change is deployed; high requires 20 hours of real manual arithmetic. Measurement and alignment time remain.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Interpret masonry drawings and calculate material requirements

steps.what: Interpret blueprints and drawings and extract verified dimensions, materials and opening details
Calculate masonry material quantities, deductions and waste allowances from verified drawing inputs
Check quantities against the drawings and accept the materials requirement

tasks.design: Use a checked quantity workbook in {SPREADSHEET} for fixed arithmetic on dimensions extracted by the brickmason from {DOCS}. Keep drawing interpretation, waste assumptions and final completeness checks with the brickmason; no model reads drawings unattended.
tasks.previous_blocker: Area deductions and unit conversions are repeatedly calculated by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: Native spreadsheet formulas can apply explicit quantity rules.
tasks.still_hard: Drawing omissions, different wall types and nonstandard openings need interpretation.
tasks.human_edge: The brickmason understands what must actually be built and detects missing scope.
tasks.altitude: Less arithmetic; no transfer of design or purchasing authority.

reach.learn: Quantity assumptions and drawing revision control

evidence.claim: Explicit area, unit-conversion and allowance formulas can calculate quantities from verified dimensions; the savings are an unmeasured E1 scenario.

assumptions: Boundary is drawing interpretation through accepted quantities, excluding ordering, deliveries and physical masonry work. Drawings are existing engineering outputs with unchanged upstream effort.

Brickmason produces drawing revision, wall ID, lengths, heights, thickness, openings, unit dimensions, joint allowance, material type, units and chosen waste allowance in s1's full 60 hours, including workbook entry. Missing dimensions or unusual details use manual takeoff during s3.
Try native quantity formulas before custom code. Waste allowance remains a human choice; it is not inferred. Existing automatic calculations earn no saving.
unknowns: Drawing consistency and existing takeoff tools
research_questions: Can a checked workbook reproduce an independently calculated wall schedule including openings and unit conversions?

incremental.description: Maintain formulas and test changed unit or wall assumptions

approvals.approved_version: Exact drawing revision, input dimensions, allowances, formula version and material schedule; changes void acceptance

time_saved_range_pct.basis: B=100 R=75; gross 25 less 4 upkeep gives net 21. Low is existing automatic takeoff arithmetic with no new change; high requires 25 hours of observed hand arithmetic and unchanged drawing interpretation.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Reduce repeated geometry and quantity arithmetic while retaining drawing interpretation and physical layout checks.
reach: Help supervisors review masonry quantity assumptions
Explain site-layout discrepancies to construction supervisors
role.ambitious_version: A brickmason who spends less time repeating arithmetic and keeps attention on site conditions and complete material scope.
